summary: Lit in 1907 on Kains Island (formerly Entrance Island) at the mouth of Quatsino Sound; keepers' home since 1910, still staffed.

structures.type: temporary light in a small enclosed wooden tower
two-storey wooden keepers' house with octagonal iron lantern on the hipped roof
white cylindrical tower (replaced the wooden lighthouse)

staffing.basis: Remote staffed lightstation with two permanent positions in the Senate committee's 2010 appendix; LighthouseFriends lists keepers to at least 2024.

access.note: Staffed lightstation, the keepers' home and workplace, owned by the Canadian Coast Guard. Reached by kayak or boat from Winter Harbour. Tower closed. Visitors should not land uninvited.

events.note: Dominion Government sets the island aside as a lighthouse site (29 June 1905)
Temporary light on the south-east end of the island: fixed white dioptric light of the seventh order, 27 m (90 ft) high; LighthouseFriends calls it a 31-day Wigham light
The 31-day Wigham lamp replaced by a dioptric 5th-order fixed white light in a new lighthouse
Permanent station: two-storey wooden keepers' house with octagonal iron lantern, finished December 1910
Visitor Walter Peterson drowned offshore when his skiff capsized, 19 December 1913
New fog alarm at Entrance Island put in operation 10 December 1923 (LighthouseFriends dates it to 1924)
Keeper Sydney Warren drowned 23 October 1929 after a wave swamped his skiff
White cylindrical tower replaced the wooden lighthouse

corrections.why: The present white cylindrical tower replaced the wooden lighthouse in 1977 (LighthouseFriends). 1905 is the year the site was set aside; the first light was 1907 (Marine report, 1908) and the permanent station was built in 1910 (Marine report, 1911).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kains Island (current Coast Guard list) and Entrance Island (government reports of 1907 and 1923-24) are the same island. LighthouseFriends dates the renaming to about 1898, but the reports kept the older name for decades. The Entrance Island off Nanaimo is a different station.
The fiscal 1923-24 report gives 10 December 1923 as the date the new fog alarm was put in operation. LighthouseFriends dates the fog alarm to 1924. The story follows the Department's date.

The report published 1908 calls the 1907 light a 31-day Wigham light and gives its optic as fixed white dioptric of the seventh order; LighthouseFriends uses the Wigham name. The report published 1911 applies the Wigham name to the lamp it replaced. The sources agree; the story reports them together.
The Wikidata figure of 12.0 m is not supported by the Coast Guard list, which gives 28.4 m above water.

The record's Lighthouse Directory note says the site is closed to visitors. LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower closed. The story reports LighthouseFriends and advises against landing uninvited.

notes_for_editor: The keeper roster comes from LighthouseFriends' 'Head Keepers' line only; no USLHS roster exists for Canada. The keepers' entries for G. H. Jackson (Marine report published 1909, printed p. 191) and N. C. Nelson (Marine report published 1913, printed p. 74) were matched by row in OCR tables and checked on the page images, which show Quatsino Light / G. H. Jackson (appointed 29 January 1907) and Quatsino / N. C. Nelson (appointed 6 December 1910). The other keepers are LighthouseFriends' alone. The Victoria Colonist account of Sadler (1918) was not read; the story gives only LighthouseFriends' summary, and the wife's illness is described in general terms. Names after about 1960 (Collins to Magee) appear only in the roster, as the published page prints them, in public role. The record's 'Kains Island' alias and 'Entrance Island' in the Marine reports are the same island; no other Entrance Island is involved. The 1957 Marine volumes beyond 1924 are not in the corpus, so the 1977 tower rests on LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard list. The 2024 Coast Guard release named in the record was not read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1909 (printed p. 191) and 1913 (printed p. 74) keeper rows were checked on the page images; the 1908 report's Wigham wording, the 1911 report's replacement sentence and the 1923-24 fog-alarm date were checked against the OCR text; Coast Guard List of Lights No. 68 was checked (Fl W 5s, 28.4 m, 18 NM, white cylindrical tower).
